conventions.convention: Complex norms have finite real values and satisfy absolute homogeneity for every complex scalar; nonnegativity is redundant rather than a separate axiom.
Complex modulus on the canonical real embedding equals real absolute value.
Realification retains the underlying set, addition, norm values and induced metric d_N(u,v)=N(u-v).
Coordinates are indexed by j<n, including n=0; the empty sum is zero and C^0 is the singleton zero space.
A complex normed subspace carries the restriction of the ambient norm and is closed under every complex scalar.
Equivalent complex norms are compared on the same complex vector space using positive real constants c,C and cM(v)≤N(v)≤CM(v) for every v.

load_bearing.statement: A complex norm on a complex vector space V is a function N:V→R separating zero, satisfying N(λv)=|λ|_C N(v) for every complex scalar λ, and satisfying N(u+v)≤N(u)+N(v).

Let (V,N) be a complex normed space and define d_N(u,v):=N(u-v) for u,v∈V. On the realification V_R, the same function N is a real norm. The underlying set, addition, norm values, and induced metric d_N are unchanged.
For every real r, write λ_r for its canonical image in C. Then |λ_r|_C=|r|_R.
Let (V,N) be a complex normed space and let W⊆V be a complex-linear subspace. Define the restricted norm N_W:W→R by N_W(w):=N(w). The pair (W,N_W) is the complex normed subspace determined by W.
For every n∈N, on the complex function space C^n with pointwise operations, N_1(z):=Σ_{j<n}|z_j|_C is a complex norm, including at n=0, when C^0 is the singleton zero space.

seams_checked.note: The consumer lemma's F1, F3 and F9 faithfully use the restricted complex norm, realification theorem and full complex homogeneity definition. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 apply them to both ambient space and subspace and retain exactly the restricted ambient metric. The supplier page promises these same interfaces; the consumer's finite-basis clause assumes a supplied basis and does not attribute basis existence to this page.
